newsitem.title: FRANCE: L'Oreal shares weak ahead of H1 results.
newsitem.headline: L'Oreal shares weak ahead of H1 results.

text.p: Shares in cosmetics group L'Oreal were weak on Thursday for a second day ahead of the company's half-year results, due after the market's close at 1500 GMT.

Analysts cited an agency report that said the group's nine-month sales were up 12 percent at 44.6 billion francs but that full-year profit would not rise as fast. "If that's true, it would be disappointing," an analyst said.

Another analyst said he thought the profit growth forecast in the report was wrong unless it included an exceptional charge. L'Oreal declined to comment on the report and said it had not issued nine-month sales results.
Its shares were down 0.4 percent at 1,777 francs at 1020 GMT after falling 2.51 percent on Wednesday.
The 1996 earnings-per-share consensus forecast for L'Oreal is 56.80 francs, up 12.5 percent from the 1995 result.

There is no half-year consensus estimate, but several analysts told Reuters they expect profit before tax, profit-sharing and capital gains/losses of just over three billion francs, or between 2.98 billion and 3.15 billion, compared with 2.75 billion in the first half of 1995.
Analysts say the 1996 half-year results will not be completely comparable due to the acquisitions of cosmetics firms Jade in Germany and Maybelline of the United States in the second half of 1995.
